done.why: I hit the 250-turn limit on my way up the chimney with the painting, one room away from the trophy case. A lot of my turns went on two deaths to the troll, fetching my scattered gear back afterward, wandering the coal-mine maze, and carrying one treasure up the chimney per trip.

about: It's the white house and the Great Underground Empire again, with changes. You collect treasures and bring them back to the trophy case. This version adds or changes a few things: after you die, your gear gets scattered around the house and a tidy someone puts the lamp back. The trap door gets barred behind you every time you go down. The round room has cave-ins. The mirror rubs you between two nearly identical rooms. The stairs to Hades are chalked shut, and the chimney is the only way back up, fitting you, your lamp and one other thing.

moments.note: Troll took my head off after three fair exchanges. The fight felt like pure luck.
The death text was new: plain things strewn about the forest, valuables rolled into dark corners, and 'somebody tidy' put the lamp back. I liked it.
Second troll death. I'd lost the sword twice mid-fight and had to keep picking it up.
Turned out the sword was lying at North of House and I walked right past it earlier. Recovering everything was a slog.
Troll finally killed in two blows on the third try.
Round Room's passages are mostly blocked by cave-ins. Different from what I remembered.
The bat grabbed me and dropped me at Ladder Top. Fun, and it got me into the mine.
Couldn't get through the narrow passage even holding only the lamp, so I had to work out the basket/light problem without a second light source.
Found my way out of the nondescript coal-mine rooms into the Gas Room with a sapphire bracelet.
The Hades staircase sealed with CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE and something laughing beyond it. Great line.
The thief robbed me blind of the bracelet, figurine and trident in a single turn. Three treasures gone.
Opening the sluice gates with the wrench worked, and the reservoir drained to reveal the trunk.
The chimney spelled out exactly what I was carrying and its rule: you, your lamp and one thing more. A clear, fair constraint.
Even after I got out by the chimney, the trap door slammed and got barred again, so every treasure meant a full round trip.

wished: I wished I could fight the troll with some sense that skill or preparation mattered, not just repeated dice rolls.
I wished the trap door would stay open once I'd found another way out, so I could bring treasures home in one trip.
I wished I had a second light source so I could do the basket-and-coal puzzle at the narrow passage.
I wished I could chase the thief to get back the bracelet, figurine and trident.
I wished the coal-mine rooms had something to tell them apart, or that I could mark them.

lines.line: The plain things are strewn about the forest and the fields around the house, anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: A new, slightly funny death penalty. It told me exactly what work I had ahead.

lines.line: Across the third step somebody has laid a slab of rock, and on it, chalked in a neat hand, CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE. Something on the far side of the notice laughs.
lines.why: The best prose in the game. A firm, atmospheric way to close off an area.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It set the rule for my whole treasure-shuttling strategy.

lines.line: The thief just left, still carrying his large bag. You may not have noticed that he robbed you blind first.
lines.why: It cost me three treasures in a single turn.

fun.why: Clearing the troll, the bat ride and draining the dam felt good. The two troll deaths, the thief's robbery and the trap door barring every time ate up the fun.

engagement.why: I always had a clear next goal: find treasure, open the way, get it home. I stayed driven right up to the cap.

difficulty.why: Luck-based combat, a thief who stripped me, a barred trap door and a one-item chimney made progress expensive under a 250-turn limit. I banked only 3 treasures (egg, trunk, and nearly the painting).

interestingness.why: The changes were genuinely interesting: tidy-lamp resurrection, cave-ins, the mirror swapping two lookalike rooms, the closed Hades stairs and the chimney's carrying rule.

prose.why: The new text fits the classic voice and is often witty. The Hades notice and the chimney message are standouts.
